solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unexpected blow son received in belly

indicators.note: something received in a place is taken inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
the gut is the belly

explanation.surface: A boy takes a surprise punch to the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A gust is a sudden rush of wind, a blow arriving without warning.

clue.text: Rewritten slogan on way for Russian policy

indicators.note: rewritten means set down again differently, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A political slogan is redrafted on its way to becoming Kremlin policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasnost, meaning openness, was Gorbachev's Soviet policy of greater transparency in the 1980s.

clue.text: Shilling — another twenty needed for calamari?

blocks.note: s was the abbreviation for a shilling in old British money
a quid is a pound, and a pound was twenty shillings

explanation.surface: A diner is told the calamari costs a shilling plus another twenty.
explanation.walkthrough: In pre-1971 British money a pound (slang: quid) was worth twenty shillings.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamari is squid prepared as food, usually fried rings.

clue.text: The Saint strangely indecisive

indicators.note: done strangely means done in an odd way, so these letters come out in an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A holy figure behaves oddly, unable to make up their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hesitant wavers before acting, which is the same as being unable to decide.

clue.text: Continental marriage? We're no longer in it

definitions.text: Continental marriage? We're no longer in it

blocks.note: surface reading: a wedding between people from mainland Europe
setter's reading: the union of European states that Britain left after Brexit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Continental' means of mainland Europe and 'marriage' is a union; 'we' is Britain, which left in 2020.
explanation.definitionFit: The political and economic bloc of European countries is a union, which the UK exited through Brexit.

clue.text: Playwright's quietly leaving Bury

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so a letter departs from the name

blocks.note: Harold Pinter was an English playwright
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A dramatist slips away quietly from a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury a body in the ground.

clue.text: A leading monk, upstanding character in theory

blocks.note: taken as written
a prior is a monk who heads a priory
the letter I stands upright, like a person

explanation.surface: A senior monk is, in principle, a person of upright character.
explanation.definitionFit: A priori reasoning works from theory and deduction rather than observed experience.

clue.text: Precious little time — almost seven days!

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: T is the short form of time
a week is seven days

explanation.surface: Someone complains of having precious little time, barely a week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precious little' reads as a phrase meaning hardly any, but 'Precious' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Precious in the sense of affectedly dainty or over-refined is what twee means.

clue.text: Stick lands regularly at this spot

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of lands
here means at this place

explanation.surface: A pilot's plane keeps landing at the same place.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick to something is to cling or adhere to it.

clue.text: In pieces like subordinate?

blocks.note: as means like, in a comparison
someone under another is subordinate to them

explanation.surface: A broken-down junior employee asks whether that is what being subordinate means.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split: the answer reads as two words, 'as under', meaning like a subordinate.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn asunder means split apart into separate fragments, the same as in pieces.

clue.text: Ultimately elegant Irish language crisply brief

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the next word is taken

blocks.note: the last letter of elegant
Erse is the old name for Irish Gaelic

explanation.surface: An Irish speaker's elegant style turns out to be short and sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: A terse remark is short and abrupt, using few words in a clipped manner.

clue.text: Jog back for one horse

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, for one
a dun is a greyish-brown horse

explanation.surface: A rider asks for a horse that can trot gently back.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone is to give them a gentle push, just as a nudge is.

clue.text: Polly run over in neighbourhood

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the word that follows

blocks.note: part of town is a neighbourhood
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A pet called Polly gets hit by a car in the local streets.
explanation.walkthrough: Polly is the stock name for a pet parrot, as in 'Polly wants a cracker'.
explanation.definitionFit: Polly is the traditional name given to a pet parrot, so the name stands for the bird.

clue.text: Is this what can make us single?

definitions.text: Is this what can make us single?

indicators.note: to make something is to form it from materials, so the letters are fashioned into a new word

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rueful question about why we stay unattached.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: unattractiveness may keep us single, and the letters of 'us single' make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unattractive might keep someone unmarried, so ugliness is a wry reason for staying single.

clue.text: Riled bears with disconcerting show of aggression

indicators.note: riled means stirred up and agitated, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
something rattling is unsettling, disconcerting

explanation.surface: Angry bears put on an unnerving display of hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabre-rattling is a threatening display of military power without actual fighting.

clue.text: Fish from lake carried in straw hat

indicators.note: something carried in a hat sits inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for lake
a boater is a flat-topped straw hat

explanation.surface: An angler carries a fish from the lake in a straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloater is a whole herring or mackerel that has been salted and smoked.

clue.text: Sailor Brown checked Scottish cloth

blocks.note: a tar is a sailor
tan is a light brown

explanation.surface: A seaman named Brown inspected some fabric from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'checked' reads as a verb for Brown's action, but it describes the cloth's pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartan is woollen fabric woven in a criss-cross pattern of Scottish clans.

clue.text: Japanese island hard on footwear we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the word is taken by how it is spoken

blocks.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
taken as written
a shoe is footwear

explanation.surface: A Japanese island is tough on shoes, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Honshu is the largest of Japan's main islands, home to Tokyo.

clue.text: Keep quiet about fate and sin

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: sh is a command to keep quiet
one's lot is one's fate

explanation.surface: Advice to stay silent about destiny and wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth, or idleness, is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Teacher's pet, last to be expelled

indicators.note: the final letter is thrown out, so the word loses its end

blocks.note: a rabbit is a common pet

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher's favourite pupil is the last one thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teacher's pet' reads as the favourite pupil; the 's is just 'is' joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish scholar and religious leader whose role is teaching the law.

clue.text: Scots child I housed in farm building

indicators.note: housed in means sheltered inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a barn is a farm building

explanation.surface: A Scottish youngster is sheltered in a barn.
explanation.definitionFit: Bairn is the Scottish and northern English word for a child.

clue.text: Bolt to glide smoothly when lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting something raises it upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to flow is to move along smoothly

explanation.surface: A bolt slides smoothly when raised, as on a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' looks like a door fastening, but it is the verb meaning to eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt food is to gulp it down fast, which is to wolf it.

clue.text: Best supplied with ball on both United wings?

indicators.note: something on both sides of another flanks it, so one piece wraps around the other
wings are the two flanks, so the outer piece sits at each edge of the inner one

blocks.note: a ball is round like the letter O, used once on each side
Utd is the usual abbreviation of United in football club names

explanation.surface: A football team does best when given the ball out on both wings.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to beat them, which is what outdoing them means.

clue.text: See silver found in island excavation

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so one piece sits within the rest

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for island
a mine is a dug-out excavation
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone spots silver turning up in a dig on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: To see something in the mind's eye is to picture it, which is imagining.

clue.text: Tennis shot from pro: European worker

blocks.note: being pro something means being for it
E is the abbreviation for European
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A shot played by a European tennis professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pro' looks like a tennis professional in the surface, but it means in favour of.
explanation.definitionFit: A forehand is a tennis stroke played with the palm facing the direction of the swing.

clue.text: Stops goals

blocks.note: first meaning: finishes or ceases, as a verb
second meaning: aims or objectives, as a noun

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a goalkeeper's saves, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb meaning finishes and as a plural noun meaning purposes or aims.
